title: FactorEngine Program-Level LLM Factor Mining on H198 Universe
description: Implement the FactorEngine framework (Lin et al., arXiv:2603.16365, March 2026) for alpha factor mining on the H198 30-stock large-cap universe. FactorEngine casts factors as Turing-complete code and separates: (i) logic revision from parameter optimization; (ii) LLM-guided directional search from Bayesian hyperparameter search; (iii) LLM API usage from local computation. Three innovations enable scale: (a) Knowledge-Infused Bootstrapping — transforms unstructured financial reports and academic papers into executable factor programs via a multi-agent extraction-verification-code-generation pipeline; (b) Experience Knowledge Base — trajectory-aware factor refinement that avoids re-exploring failed directions; (c) Dual-mode factor code generation: 'revise' (modify existing factor code with LLM) vs. 'generate' (new factor from market logic). Implementation: (1) Feed FactorEngine our hypothesis-log.md as the initial knowledge base (we have 380+ factor hypotheses with results); (2) Let it generate candidate factor programs for the H198 universe; (3) Run backtest evaluation loop; (4) Select top survivors. Gate: OOS Sharpe > 1.174, at least one generated factor achieves IC > 0.05 OOS. IS: 2013-2020, OOS: 2021-2026. Cost: ~$20-50 OpenAI for generation passes. Script: backtesting/daily/run_h382_factorengine.py (to be written).
rationale: FactorEngine's 'knowledge-infused bootstrapping' module is uniquely suited to our situation — we have a rich hypothesis-log with 380+ factor experiments, each with results and failure reasons. This is exactly the 'experience knowledge base' FactorEngine is designed to exploit. Rather than starting blind, it starts with the accumulated knowledge of which signals work (H376 6-0m, H343 OB filter, H215 alpha101) and which fail (H291 52w-high, H337 quality), enabling targeted exploration of adjacent promising signals. This is a direct operationalization of the dream cycle research process — automated hypothesis generation from prior results. FactorEngine is distinct from AlphaLogics (H381): FactorEngine is code/program-level with Bayesian HPO; AlphaLogics is logic/abstraction-level with LLM-guided search.
